case_title: SHER SINGH & ANR. v. STATE OF HARYANA
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple fractures, injuries on vital parts, heavy bleeding, intent to kill
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced under s.302/149, 323/149 and 148 IPC
high_court_outcome: Converted conviction to s.304 (Part II)/149 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, several individuals, attacked the victim and his wife and son while they were harvesting their crop. The accused used weapons such as an axe, bankri, jailli, and lathis. The victim was dragged to a tubewell and left there to bleed. The victim later succumbed to his injuries at a hospital. The accused claimed there was a dispute over land, and they were defending themselves against the victim's attack. The prosecution presented evidence from eyewitnesses and medical reports indicating the victim sustained severe injuries, including fractures and internal bleeding, which were sufficient to cause death. The trial court convicted several accused of murder, while others were acquitted. The High Court initially reduced the conviction to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, finding the intent to kill was evident.
